questions.stem: Where does Dynamic Data Masking (DDM) apply its masking?
options: Permanently at rest in the datastore
In transit, on the fly, so the data in the datastore is unchanged
In a separate copy of the production database
Only in backups
Only in development environments
questions.explanation: DDM does not mask permanently; it masks data in transit so the data in the datastore stays unchanged.

questions.stem: What proportion of data is described as structured data, compared with the semi-structured and unstructured data of the new era?
questions.explanation: Previously work was on structured data only, which is 20%, whereas the new era adds 80% more data in semi-structured and unstructured form.

questions.stem: Why has Dynamic Data Masking become popular?
options: Because with 80% more semi-structured and unstructured data it became troublesome to anonymise data within a given SLA using static masking
Because regulators banned Static Data Masking
Because it requires no computing resources
Because it permanently deletes sensitive data
Because structured data no longer needs masking
questions.explanation: The growth of semi-structured and unstructured data and maturing data science practices made slow static masking hard to deliver within SLA, so DDM masks production data on the fly.

questions.stem: Which masking approach requires a copy of production data to be made before masking?
options: Dynamic Data Masking
Both SDM and DDM
Static Data Masking
Neither SDM nor DDM
Only DDM when run in real time
questions.explanation: SDM makes a copy of production data somewhere else before masking, whereas DDM uses the same production data because masking is done on the fly.

questions.stem: How do SDM and DDM differ in when the masking is processed?
options: Both are real-time
Both are batch
SDM is real-time and DDM is batch
SDM is done weekly and DDM monthly
SDM is done in batches which take time, whereas DDM is real-time
questions.explanation: SDM is done in batches that take time to process, whereas DDM is real-time.

questions.stem: Why does Dynamic Data Masking carry an additional performance requirement?
options: Because it copies the whole database every night
Because it runs along with every SQL statement sent to the datastore
Because it must re-index every table
Because it stores masked data in a second datastore
Because it encrypts the data at rest
questions.explanation: SDM has no additional performance requirement because it is done once, whereas DDM runs with every SQL sent to the datastore.

questions.stem: How is Static Data Masking run, compared with Dynamic Data Masking?
options: SDM is a permanent layer and DDM a standalone process
Both are permanent layers
Both are standalone processes
SDM is a standalone process, whereas DDM is a permanent layer before exposing data to users
SDM runs inside the application and DDM inside the database
questions.explanation: SDM is done as a standalone process, whereas DDM is a permanent layer sitting before the data is exposed to users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Dynamic Data Masking?
options: It permanently changes the data at rest
It masks data in transit
It uses the same production data rather than a copy
It is real-time
It behaves like standard Data Masking in what it does to the values
questions.explanation: It is SDM that masks data permanently at rest and cannot be reverted; DDM leaves the datastore unchanged.

questions.stem: Which group's maturing practices have increased the demand for production-ready masked data?
options: Network engineers
Auditors
Data Scientists developing, training and publishing models
Marketing teams
Help desk staff
questions.explanation: Data science practices have matured over the last ten years, so more production-ready data is required by Data Scientists to develop, train and publish their models.

questions.stem: Why is Static Data Masking described as a very slow process?
options: Because it runs with every SQL query
Because it must be approved by regulators each time
Because it works only on unstructured data
Because it masks data in transit
Because one must create a new dataset containing the masked data
questions.explanation: With SDM one must create a new dataset with masked data, whereas DDM masks production data on the fly.
